meta.publisher_metric: Harmonic mean of recall and precision.

scorecard.scoring_note: Percentile ranks are computed inside one unit. Capability and stage scores are weighted means over present observations only; missing weight is reported, never redistributed.

strengths: Freshness is not a concern: every scored unit reports snapshot_age_days 0 against max_snapshot_age_days 30, and the swebench-multilingual/multimodal boards report 0 against max_snapshot_age_days 90.

Operational fields are complete and attributed: each route carries input_price, output_price and context_limit with source '~/.pi/agent/models-store.json' and a read_at timestamp one day before reference_time, so no price or limit is asserted without provenance.

The scorecard is conservative about eligibility: run_stage_plan, review_plan and general carry signal 'no_comparable_evidence' rather than a fabricated ranking, and their rows are all eligible false with rank null.
Proxy evidence is explicitly downgraded rather than used: opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash's deepswe entry is recorded as 'proxy-family (deliberately not scored)' for publisher 'deepseek-v4-flash'.

Implement's tie handling is transparent and does not overclaim: the rank-1 tie group states 'Capability ranks remain tied' and labels the resolution 'cost-broke-tie', keeping the operational preference separate from capability.

Coverage is reported with missing weight named per capability and never redistributed, so partial rows (for example mistral/zai-glm-5-2 at coverage 0.5 in implement, missing tool_use 0.3 and repository_understanding 0.2) are auditable.
risks: Evidence base is three units only (deepswe population_size 28, tbench-v2.1 population_size 14, codereviewbench population_size 13); swebench-multilingual is scored but contributes no route evidence, and all three swebench-multimodal units are 'small-board-excluded'.

Half the plan is unevaluated: run_stage_plan, review_plan and general show coverage 0 for all nine routes, so the three baselines opencode-go/glm-5.3, openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol and openai-codex/gpt-5.6-luna are unvalidated in those roles.

Every stage that does have eligible candidates has an unrankable baseline (implement baseline_coverage 0, review baseline_coverage 0.3, run_stage_break baseline_coverage 0), so no candidate rank is measured against the incumbent it would replace.

run_stage_break has a single eligible route; that winner's missing capability is adversarial_analysis at weight 0.4, the stage's largest weight, so its rank 1 rests on 0.6 coverage without its dominant capability observed.

review-stage ranks 2 through 4 sit at coverage 0.5 with software_engineering (0.3) and reasoning (0.2) unobserved, i.e. half the stage weight drives the ordering, and codereviewbench publishes uncertainty null so no interval bounds those percentiles.

The two gpt-5.6-luna routes share identical percentiles on both boards under the alias rule 'Published release is served by two providers; both routes claim this release', so the evidence cannot separate openai-codex from opencode-go even though their context limits differ (272000 vs 1050000).
contested_tolerance is documented as 'not yet applied to the gap between two routes in a stage', so apparent neighbour gaps inside a stage are unresolved by the scorecard's own admission.
disqualifiers: No routing change is supported for any of the six stages: three report 'no_comparable_evidence' and three report 'baseline_unrankable' with the rationale 'eligible candidates are listed without a baseline comparison'. Coverage is too low to decide, in every stage.

run_stage_break cannot be reassigned on this evidence: the only eligible candidate is missing the stage's 0.4-weight capability, and the incumbent opencode-go/hy3 has baseline_coverage 0, leaving the stage with no comparison at all.

general is disqualified from any judgement: all four weighted capabilities (instruction_following 0.3, reasoning 0.3, long_context 0.2, multimodal 0.2) are missing for every route, so the default route has zero measured weight.
divergence: The implement rank-1 tie group lists openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol (score 0.7745535714285714) and opencode-go/glm-5.3 (score 0.734375) as tied while their composites differ by less than contested_tolerance 0.05; I read the 'cost-broke-tie' selection of glm-5.3 as a price/context preference, not as evidence that it matches or exceeds sol on capability, especially given sol's output_price 30 versus glm-5.3's 4.4.

opencode-go/kimi-k2.7-code takes review rank 1 from a single unit (codereviewbench, population_size 13, uncertainty null) while the deepswe population contains 'kimi-k2-7-code' at percentile 0.08928571428571429 that route_evidence does not claim under any alias_rule; the review leadership therefore rests on the narrowest base available and excludes a same-name agentic observation.

implement reports baseline_coverage 0 for opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash even though route_evidence holds a scored codereviewbench observation for it; that is a stage-definition artifact, and I would not read it as the model having no evidence, only none for this stage.

mistral/zai-glm-5-2 is scored in implement at coverage 0.5 from one deepswe observation whose percentile 0.16071428571428573 sits near the bottom of that 28-model board, so its rank 3 is an ordering among sparse rows rather than a demonstrated capability level.

review's baseline openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol is reported with coverage 0.3 and missing the stage's own highest-weight capability 'review' (0.5); the scorecard correctly withholds a comparison, but I diverge from any reading that treats the incumbent review route as confirmed adequate.

I do not treat the absence of evidence in run_stage_plan, review_plan and general as evidence of baseline adequacy or inadequacy; the scorecard's 'no rank' is a measurement gap, and the three incumbent routes should be logged as unevaluated rather than retained with confidence.

fixtures.planted_defect: A stage ranks a route whose coverage is below rank_threshold_coverage, even though the rules forbid a rank below the threshold.
A family-level observation (source_scope proxy-family) is presented inside the scored observations, which promotes proxy evidence to a routed result.
Two observations from different units are averaged into one figure, which the rules forbid because values are only comparable inside one unit.

calibration.detection_note: Keyword detection is a proxy. It shows the judge addressed the planted defect, not that its wording or reasoning was correct.

recommendations.rationale: Every route has 0% coverage of this stage. repository_understanding, reasoning, long_context, and instruction_following have no tier A source, so no route can be ranked and the configured chain is unchanged for lack of evidence, not for lack of merit. Do not read this as support for the current chain.

Every route has 0% coverage. reasoning and adversarial_analysis have no tier A source and repository_understanding is unmeasured, so plan review cannot be ranked by published data. Local plan samples remain the only route to evidence for this stage.

openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol (0.775) and opencode-go/glm-5.3 (0.734) tie for rank 1 within the 0.05 tolerance, and opencode-go/glm-5.3 dominates on both input and output price (1.40/4.40 against 5.00/30.00 USD per million tokens). It is a candidate to add as an implementation secondary. This is additive: the configured rank 1, opencode-go/deepseek-v4.1-flash, is unrankable here because its only software-engineering observation is proxy-family and unscored, so it cannot be compared and must not be replaced on this evidence. The configured ranks 2 and 3 already match the attested rank-2 group.

The configured rank 1, openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol, has no review observation at all: it covers only 30% of this stage through software_engineering and is evidence-only. Four enabled routes carry review evidence, led by opencode-go/kimi-k2.7-code at 0.885 with a 0.154 gap to the next candidate, well above the separation tolerance. Recommend moving opencode-go/kimi-k2.7-code to rank 1 and keeping openai-codex/gpt-5.6-sol at rank 2, so the stage gains its primary capability without losing the incumbent. Apply only after the validation step in section 9: the evidence is one vendor harness at 50% coverage, judged by one LLM whose rescoring noise is about 2 points, and absence of a published row for the incumbent is missing evidence, not proof of worse review.

mistral/zai-glm-5-2 is the only route that reaches the coverage threshold for this stage (0.407 at 60%), so it is worth adding as a break secondary. Read it narrowly: adversarial_analysis carries 0.4 of the stage and has no tier A source, so 60% of the rank comes from review and software_engineering. The configured rank 1, opencode-go/hy3, has 0% coverage and cannot be assessed either way.

No route has evidence for instruction_following, reasoning, long_context, or multimodal with which this stage is weighted, so the session-start model cannot be ranked. Its 0.20/1.20 price and 272K context are operational facts, not routing-quality results.

probe.result: HTTP 200, 94 KB JSON, key 'rows' with 70 configurations over 28 models, generated_at 2026-09-03

caveats: Every row uses the same harness (mini-swe-agent), so a result is agent-model-system evidence unless the model effect is isolated.
Rows repeat a model at several reasoning efforts; the scorer keeps the highest published effort and records the alternatives.
Pass rates carry published run-to-run intervals (ci_lo, ci_hi); the pipeline records them and never combines them statistically.
Trajectory-level analysis is not published as data, so this source scores software_engineering only, not repository_understanding or long_context.

benchmarks.name: Terminal-Bench v2.1
benchmarks.licence: site content; run logs are published separately by the maintainers

probe.result: HTTP 200; 18 ranked rows inside the React Server Component flight payload; accuracy, accuracy_ci95_half_width, n_trials, pass_at_k published per row

caveats: The rows are JSON inside the server-rendered flight payload, not a documented JSON endpoint. The adapter extracts the rows array and fails loudly if the shape changes.
Rows are agent+model+effort configurations; results are agent-model-system evidence.
The board has 13 distinct models after dedupe, so the scorer marks it small-board.
There is no public per-task results file for this board: the Hugging Face submissions dataset stores per-task rollout directories, which is not a machine-readable leaderboard.

benchmarks.name: SWE-bench Multimodal

probe.result: HTTP 200; Multimodal board has 22 rows across 12 agent harnesses; 21 rows marked checked

caveats: Task inputs include screenshots and UI images, so this is the only tier A source for the multimodal capability.
Rows split across three harness classes; only the agent-cli class reaches 7 distinct models, which the scorer excludes as a small board.
Probed 2026-09-11: no evaluated route in the current candidate set appears on this board.
Several rows belong to the 2025 model generation and show a wide spread between harnesses, so scores are agent-model-system evidence.

benchmarks.name: CodeReviewBench
benchmarks.licence: not stated as a licence name; the payload's licence field points at the code repository https://github.com/kodustech/codereviewbench

probe.result: HTTP 200, schema.org Dataset JSON, key 'models' with 13 ranked models over 30 pull requests and 95 confirmed bugs, generatedAt 2026-09-11; the bare host answers 307, so the fetch URL pins www

caveats: Every ranked entry runs on the publisher's own review harness, so a row is agent-model-system evidence, not model evidence.

The publisher is an AI code-review vendor scoring its own harness, and the ranked set is a curation: probed 2026-09-18, gpt-5.6-luna and gpt-5.6-terra have 30-case scorecards in the repository but no leaderboard row, so absence from this board is not evidence of poor review ability.

Findings are matched to human review comments by a single LLM judge (claude-haiku-4-5). Probed 2026-09-18, rescoring one unchanged kimi-k2.7-code submission moved F1 from 0.4311 to 0.4108 across two scoring dates, about 2 points, which exceeds the gap between adjacent ranks. That noise is recorded here and never combined statistically with a score.
The payload publishes no confidence interval, so a row records uncertainty as null and adjacent ranks are not an ordering claim.
One review pass per model at vendor defaults; no reasoning-effort variation is published, so effort is null and the board cannot separate effort.

The payload does not state the benchmark version, and the publisher also runs a heavy variant. The registry records light-v1, verified from the per-model scorecards on 2026-09-18; a version bump would not be detected automatically.
The metric is micro-averaged F1, verified against the per-model scorecards on 2026-09-18: the payload value is the scorecard f1Micro rounded to one decimal.

benchmarks.name: ContextBench

probe.result: HTTP 200; the leaderboard table ships as a literal array inside a Turbopack chunk (model, performance.file/block/line precision+recall+f1, pass_at_1, patterns, dynamics). No JSON export, no documented API. The repository publishes task data (parquet/csv) but no result file.

benchmarks.reason: Results exist but are embedded as JavaScript module literals, not JSON. Extracting them needs a JavaScript parser, so the source stays evidence-only under the adapter rule.
caveats: Agent-model-system evidence: it measures context selection inside one trajectory, not general repository understanding.
The page separates bare-model rows from mini-SWE-agent rows, which maps well to the model versus agent-model-system distinction, but the pipeline cannot read it yet.

One benchmark currently covers both repository_understanding and long_context. Enabling this source without changing the property model would count one retrieval measurement twice in the run_stage_plan vector (0.3 and 0.2). Decide the property model before promoting it.
Promotion path: a dedicated adapter that parses the chunk literal and asserts every entry has model and performance.file.f1. It needs a fixture test and loud failure on shape change.

benchmarks.name: SWE Atlas (QnA, Test Writing, Refactoring)

probe.result: HTTP 200. The flight payload carries methodology prose (scored by an LLM judge, Task Resolve Rate) but no rows. Rows are loaded client-side; no JSON endpoint found.

benchmarks.reason: No machine-readable result export. An LLM judge grades rubrics, so the top-level number also mixes judge behaviour with model behaviour.
caveats: QnA, Test Writing, and Refactoring are separate boards; treat them as separate units if a source ever becomes readable.
Needs a JavaScript runtime or an undocumented API, both outside the adapter rule.

benchmarks.name: SWE-bench ProMax
benchmarks.reason: Excluded from the pipeline: tasks are mined from public commits and results stay scaffold-sensitive.
caveats: Secondary at most. Better curation and scale do not remove contamination exposure.

benchmarks.name: SWE-bench Pro
benchmarks.reason: Excluded from the pipeline: a published audit found widespread task and verifier defects.
caveats: Secondary at most. Use only with the audit caveat stated.

benchmarks.name: SWE-bench Verified
benchmarks.reason: Deprecated for frontier routing: contamination and saturation weaken separation. The board is still fetched for population context but no capability maps to it.
caveats: Historical context only.

benchmarks.name: c-CRAB

probe.command: no public result export located for the paper

benchmarks.reason: Closest construct fit for code review, but no fetchable result table.
caveats: Measures whether review feedback guides a fixed coding agent to pass tests derived from human-raised issues; it does not measure valid findings absent from those reviews.
Plan review still needs local samples: no coding-review benchmark establishes plan-review quality.

benchmarks.name: CR-Bench
benchmarks.reason: Reports defect precision, recall, usefulness, and signal-to-noise, but without a fetchable export.
caveats: Inherits SWE-bench provenance and uses an LLM judge; judge version and human agreement must be recorded with any result.

benchmarks.name: CyberGym

benchmarks.reason: Security-specific, and results are not exported from a first-party leaderboard.
caveats: Establishes vulnerability discovery and reproduction, not general adversarial analysis.

benchmarks.name: Aider Polyglot

probe.result: HTTP 200 HTML page; no JSON or CSV export

benchmarks.reason: Conditional short-form editing evidence, and the leaderboard is HTML only.
caveats: Editing a small file with a provided diff is not repository-scale implementation evidence.

benchmarks.name: Artificial Analysis component evaluations

probe.result: HTTP 401 without an API key; component evaluation pages are also key-gated

benchmarks.reason: Key-gated. Useful for discovery and normalisation, but the composite index must not be used as a direct score.
caveats: Prefer a component evaluation over the composite index, and record which component was used.
A knowledge or preference score is not interchangeable with a reasoning score.
